territorial_scope.description: Applies within the State of Hawaii, with the conduct test keyed to deceiving residents of the State.

evidence.quote: intends to deceive a resident of the State.

summary.short: Bans persons from recklessly distributing materially deceptive AI or deepfake media that risks harming election candidates or voter behavior, from February of each even-numbered year through the next general election, unless a prescribed disclaimer is included. Sets graded criminal penalties and civil remedies; effective on approval.
summary.long: Adds HRS §11-A barring any person from recklessly distributing, or agreeing to distribute, materially deceptive media between the first working day of February in each even-numbered year and the next general election, in reckless disregard of risks to candidates or voters. Covered media are advertisements depicting someone in speech or conduct they did not engage in, that a reasonable viewer would believe, made with AI, GAN or digital technology. Broadcasters, cable and satellite providers, and online, cloud, streaming and technology providers are largely excluded unless they helped create the media or, for online services, knew it was deceptive and intended to deceive a state resident. A prescribed disclaimer exempts media, with detailed size, placement, language and citation rules. Violations are a petty misdemeanor, a misdemeanor if repeated within five years, or a class C felony with intent to cause violence or bodily harm; the commission may assess a fine or refer cases for prosecution. Adds HRS §11-B allowing damages suits by depicted individuals, candidates and voter organizations, and injunctions sought by officials and those parties; civil fines up to $1,000 per day apply for violating injunctions. Takes effect upon approval.

notes: The supplied document is the bill text; the registry lists the stage as adopted. Section 4 says new material is underscored, but the supplied text shows no underscoring, so all of section 2 is treated as new. The commission in §11-A(g) is not defined; the only commission named in the bill is the campaign spending commission in §11-B(b)(2). §11-A(g) refers to prosecution under 'subpart I', which is not in this document. The findings mention Michigan, Minnesota and Washington statutes, but no relation to them is stated in the operative text.

"Artificial intelligence" means a machine-based system that can, for a given set of human-defined objectives, make predictions, recommendations, or decisions influencing real or virtual environments
"Cloud service provider" means a third-party company that provides scalable computing resources that businesses can access on demand over a network
"Direct-to-home satellite provider" has the same meaning as defined in title 47 United States Code section 303(v).
"Distribute" means to convey information by any means.
"Interactive computer service" has the same meaning as defined in title 47 United States Code section 230(f)(2).

obligations.summary: Any person shall not recklessly distribute, or agree with another person to distribute, materially deceptive media in reckless disregard of the risk of harming a candidate's reputation or electoral prospects or changing voters' behaviour, within the period from the first working day of February in every even-numbered year through the next general election. Exceptions in subsections (b) and (c) apply.
obligations.applies_from: between the first working day of February in every even-numbered year through the next general election
obligations.conditional_on: subject to the exceptions in subsections (b) and (c); the media is materially deceptive media as defined

evidence.quote: no person shall recklessly distribute, or enter into an agreement with another person to distribute

obligations.summary: A person relying on the disclaimer exception must include a disclaimer that the media was manipulated by technical means and depicts appearance, speech or conduct that did not occur. Format requirements apply by media type: video (throughout, clearly visible, letters at least as large as the largest text, same language), image (clearly visible, same language), audio (read at beginning and end, audible pitch, same language). Edited or newly created media derived from existing media must also cite the original sources.
obligations.conditional_on: applies only where the person seeks the exception in §11-A(c) by including a disclaimer

evidence.quote: Subsection (a) shall not apply if the media includes a disclaimer informing the viewer that the media has been manipulated by technical means
